source.title: Gradient Alignment for Cross-Domain Face Anti-Spoofing
source.authors: B. M. Le; Simon S. Woo

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including supplementary material, is present. Some flattened table entries have merged uncertainty values.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates cross-domain face anti-spoofing, an out-of-distribution setting that the claim excludes. Its experiments do not test the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports cross-domain FAS results and loss-landscape visualizations. These concern generalization to unseen domains, not the same-distribution generalization measured by the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses the flat-minimum/generalization premise to design GAC-FAS and reports its cross-domain performance. It does not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness versus training–test gap relationship or any other listed version. Cross-domain evaluation alone would not exclude a test; the measured comparisons do not match the versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors conclude that GAC-FAS improves cross-domain FAS and encourages flatter, more stable minima. Their claims of consistent superiority need qualification: Table 4 shows worse HTER and AUC than SA-FAS on OCM → I, which they describe as comparable. Landscape flatness is supported qualitatively, without testing V7's specified correlation.
record.recipe_differences: A domain-generalization method for face anti-spoofing using gradient alignment and SAM-inspired training; it does not use the claim versions' same-distribution generalization tests.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports sensitivity to γ and ρ: excessively large values may deteriorate performance; settings are shown in Figure 4.

fits_no_version.finding: GAC-FAS achieves convergence HTERs of 9.89%, 12.51%, 12.29%, and 15.37% across four held-out-domain tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Domain-wise ascending points with gradient alignment can improve cross-domain face anti-spoofing performance under the tested recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 5 qualitatively depicts a flatter training-loss landscape for GAC-FAS than four baselines on ICM → O. It provides no magnitude-aware sharpness scores or training–test gap correlation; the authors describe baseline generalization as comparable in Table 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GAC-FAS produces a visually flatter training-loss landscape than the compared FAS methods in this task.

record.problems: The supplied tables are flattened and some mean/standard-deviation values are merged. Reported experiments concern cross-domain evaluation, not the claim's same-distribution setting.
record.rows_left_out: Other cross-domain metrics and conditions in Tables 1–3 and corruption results in Figure 7 were not extracted; they concern out-of-distribution evaluation, which the prompt separates from the claim. Figure-only hyperparameter and corruption values were also not transcribed.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the corresponding natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy comparison.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error and their effects on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning. Table 5 compares sharpness-aware objectives, not this optimizer contrast.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Controlled dropout comparisons, including training-set size and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its association with measured training–test gaps among similarly fitted networks, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All four rows describe an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 trained with SGD, weight decay, and supervised contrastive regularization. Their observed states should not be interpreted as observations of any listed claim version.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and same-distribution test performance.
Width sweeps past interpolation and same-distribution test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the stated tuning conditions.
Large-batch training and same-distribution performance under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects on same-distribution test error.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and its correlation with the same-distribution training-test gap.
Removing highly memorized training examples and measuring same-distribution test accuracy.
